intended_object: The set of n-dimensional simplices (n-faces) of an abstract simplicial complex K, i.e. the faces σ ∈ K with |σ| = n + 1. This comes from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
The definition is `{σ : Face K // σ.1.card = n + 1}`. Here `Face K` is the subtype of finsets that belong to K. In Mathlib, the faces of an `AbstractSimplicialComplex` are nonempty finsets and are closed under taking nonempty subsets. So the definition picks out exactly the faces with n+1 vertices, which is the standard notion of an n-simplex of the complex. Because every face is nonempty and n + 1 ≥ 1, no degenerate empty face can appear. There are no degenerate-case problems: if K has no face of dimension n, the type is simply empty.

The definition works for any vertex type ι. The linear order is only added later in the file, for the vertex enumeration, so the definition is not narrower than it needs to be.

I searched Mathlib's `AlgebraicTopology/SimplicialComplex` and found no definition of the n-faces of an abstract simplicial complex. The name "RealizationCell" is unusual, but the docstring and the body agree.
